blockers:
**BLOCKER / ruling for Arnaud: D-57's premise does not hold in this tree, so the mechanism it names has nothing to observe and the census cannot go 23 → 21 by it.**

The measurement: (1) there is NO builder spelling for a database-side default — a declared default is `DefaultValue<T> = T | (() => T)`, every generator except `increment` installs a JavaScript closure, and admission always spells a value, so the DDL defaults the migration drivers write (`gen_random_uuid()`, `NOW()`, `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; MySQL deliberately declines `UUID()`) are never the value a row receives. The ruling's "MySQL `UUID()` default" cannot arise. (2) Both sentences therefore reduce to ONE shape, more than one `increment` column among the fields the operation must know — which is #16's shape on the batch route, KEPT by D-55. (3) That shape exists on no shipped non-RETURNING provider: MySQL is the only `supportsReturning: false` adapter and refuses a second AUTO_INCREMENT column, errno 1075 / SQLSTATE 42000, measured. (4) An AUTO_INCREMENT is precisely the brief's stated exception — a default that cannot be observed apart from its insert; the catalog's next value is a statistic, not a reservation (measured: two readers, same number). Building an adapter seam for "how a default is spelled" would ship zero implementations — dead surface, so the unit stopped at the measurement.

Three dispositions, none chosen by the author (note §6):
(a) **KEEP both**, correcting only the map's *reachable* column for rows 26 and 33 in `g4/release/plan/refusals-map.md` from "YES — smallest payload … on a non-RETURNING driver (MySQL)" to **NO on any shipped driver**. Cost nothing; census stays 23. (This map edit is a REQUESTED CHANGE in a file this unit does not own — it was not made.)
(b) **Tell them apart by construction** (N4/D-52's mechanism): both sites become `assertInvariant` (`shared/invariant.ts`), which the census counts as an invariant and not a refusal — the only route to D-57's 21. The objection to weigh: an invariant is "a state the code cannot be in when it is right, established upstream by a type or by an earlier owner", and half of what forecloses this one is a PROVIDER fact (MySQL's errno 1075), not an owner in this tree; a third-party adapter declaring `supportsReturning: false` for a provider that admits two generated columns would meet an `EngineInvariantError` where it meets a typed capability refusal today.
(c) **Add the public spelling the ruling assumes** (a database-side default, e.g. `s.string().id().dbDefault(sql`UUID()`)). That makes the observation mechanism real and worth one owner across `create`, `createMany({select})` and a nested create — and it is a public-contract change, out of scope under the common brief's stop rules.
A fourth, rejected by the author as not his call: folding the two sentences into ONE owner (they are two readers of one fact — "which fields will the provider produce, and can it name them?"). It reaches 22, not 21, and changes a registered public sentence.

No other blocker. No stop-rule condition was hit (no repeated minimized failure, no needed legacy fallback, no duplicated semantic interpretation).
